Lightforge is a native Linux client for World of Warcraft and other Battle.net games. It allows users to install, patch, verify, and launch World of Warcraft directly without the official Battle.net client, using reimplemented Blizzard distribution protocols in Rust. For other Battle.net games, it manages a single Battle.net prefix and launches the official client.

Mango is a self-hosted manga and manhwa reader built with Rust. It leverages Mihon-compatible extensions to access content from various sources and can also read local files. The application is designed to be lightweight, with a single Rust binary for the server and web UI, and extensions running in a separate, on-demand process.

Materialfy is a native desktop client for Spotify built using Rust and Qt Quick, offering a Material 3 Expressive user interface. It provides a streamlined music listening experience on Windows and Linux, with experimental support for macOS. The client integrates audio playback via librespot and dynamically adapts interface colors to the current track's album art.

SnapBack is a Windows application designed to restore your system to a desired baseline state without requiring a reboot. It intelligently identifies and closes applications that have been opened since the baseline was set, allowing them to save work politely, and optionally includes a deep memory cleanup feature.
